content: The text provided is a detailed and technical compilation of references, study results, and methodological descriptions related to the diagnosis and monitoring of Hepatitis C Virus (HCV) infection using various antigen and antibody assays. 1. Medina-Islas Y and Ruiz-Gonzalez V conducted a study comparing two diagnostic algorithms for identifying patients with HCV viremia using a novel HCV antigen test. Their findings were published in Annals of Hepatology in 2014, highlighting the potential of this new diagnostic approach. 2. Rouet F and colleagues evaluated the utility of a fourth-generation ELISA assay for reliably identifying HCV infection in HIV-positive adults in Gabon, Central Africa. Their research, published in PLoS One in 2015, demonstrated the assay's effectiveness in this specific population. 3. Russi S et al. assessed the total HCV core protein in patients with HCV-related mixed cryoglobulinemia. Their findings, published in Arthritis Research & Therapy in 2014, provided insights into the role of HCV core protein in this condition. 4. Vanhommerig JW and colleagues evaluated an HCV antigen assay for routine HCV screening among men who have sex with men (MSM) infected with HIV. Their study, published in Journal of Virological Methods in 2015, emphasized the assay's potential in this high-risk group. 5. Vermehren J et al. explored the clinical utility of the ARCHITECT HCV Ag assay for early treatment monitoring in patients with chronic HCV genotype 1 infection. Their research, published in Journal of Clinical Virology in 2012, demonstrated the assay's value in guiding therapeutic decisions. 6. Laperche S and colleagues demonstrated that simultaneous detection of HCV core antigen and anti-HCV antibodies improves early detection of HCV infection. Their study, published in Journal of Clinical Microbiology in 2005, highlighted the benefits of combined testing. 7. Nastouli E et al. compared nucleic acid testing with antibody and antigen-antibody detection methods for diagnosing acute HCV in HIV-infected patients. Their findings, published in Journal of Clinical Virology in 2009, underscored the importance of sensitive diagnostic tools in this population. 8. Vermeersch P and colleagues evaluated the use of a combined HCV antigen/antibody assay in routine laboratory practice. Their study, published in Acta Clinica Belgica in 2010, provided evidence for the assay's practical application. 9. Saito R et al. assessed the performance of an automated system for quantifying HCV core antigen. Their research, published in Journal of Virological Methods in 2003, demonstrated the system's accuracy and reliability. 10. Lu YC and colleagues investigated the clinical value of detecting HCV core antigen. Their study, published in Xi Bao Yu Fen Zi Mian Yi Xue Za Zhi in 2007, highlighted the diagnostic significance of this marker. 11. Ouyang Y et al. conducted qualitative detection of HCV core antigen in serum samples from patients with chronic hepatitis C. Their findings, published in Zhong Nan Da Xue Xue Bao Yi Xue Ban in 2006, emphasized the assay's role in chronic HCV management. 12. Zhang HQ and colleagues explored the use of HCV core antigen detection for early diagnosis of HCV infection in plasma donors in China. Their study, published in World Journal of Gastroenterology in 2007, demonstrated the assay's utility in blood safety. 13. Zhu H et al. examined the clinical significance of testing for HCV core antigen. Their findings, published in the Journal of Dalian Medical University in 2010, provided insights into its diagnostic and prognostic value. 14. El-Emshaty WM and colleagues evaluated the diagnostic performance of an immunoassay for simultaneous detection of HCV core antigen and antibodies among hemodialysis patients. Their study, published in Brazilian Journal of Microbiology in 2011, highlighted the assay's effectiveness in this vulnerable population. 15. Yang JF et al. assessed the performance characteristics of a combined HCV core antigen and anti-HCV antibody test in different patient groups. Their findings, published in Kaohsiung Journal of Medical Sciences in 2011, demonstrated the test's versatility. 16. Alzahrani AJ investigated the simultaneous detection of HCV core antigen and antibodies in Saudi drug users using a novel assay. Their study, published in Journal of Medical Virology in 2008, emphasized the assay's potential in high-risk populations. 17. Agha S et al. evaluated the reliability of an HCV core antigen assay for detecting viremia across HCV genotypes 1, 2, 3, and 4 in blood donors. Their collaborative study, published in Journal of Medical Virology in 2004, involved researchers from Japan, Egypt, and Uzbekistan. 18. El-Sayed Zaki M and El-Adrosy H proposed a recent approach for diagnosing early HCV infection. Their findings, published in Egyptian Journal of Immunology in 2004, highlighted advancements in early detection methods. 19. Letowska M et al. studied the presence of HCV core antigen in Polish blood donors. Their research, published in Transfusion in 2004, provided insights into the assay's application in blood safety. 20. Nubling CM and colleagues compared the sensitivity of HCV core antigen and HCV RNA detection during the early infection phase. Their study, published in Transfusion in 2002, emphasized the importance of early diagnostic markers. 21. Feng B et al. demonstrated that HCV core antigen is an earlier and stronger predictor of sustained virological response in patients with genotype 1 HCV infection. Their findings, published in BMC Gastroenterology in 2014, underscored its prognostic value. 22. Loggi E et al. analyzed patterns of HCV-RNA and HCV core antigen during early monitoring of standard treatment for chronic hepatitis C. Their study, published in Journal of Clinical Virology in 2013, provided insights into treatment response. 23. Moscato GA et al. quantified HCV core antigen for therapy monitoring in chronic hepatitis C. Their findings, published in Intervirology in 2011, demonstrated the assay's utility in clinical practice. 24. Fujino T et al. showed that early decline in HCV core antigen levels predicts sustained virological response in patients treated with pegylated interferon and ribavirin combination therapy. Their study, published in Journal of Digestive Diseases in 2009, highlighted its predictive value. 25. Takahashi M et al. demonstrated the benefit of HCV core antigen assay in predicting therapeutic response to interferon and ribavirin combination therapy. Their findings, published in Journal of Clinical Microbiology in 2005, emphasized its role in treatment planning. 26. Fytili P et al. reported the frequency of very low HCV viremia detected by a highly sensitive HCV-RNA assay. Their study, published in Journal of Clinical Virology in 2007, highlighted the importance of sensitive diagnostic tools.
